title: Astrid and the Visitor
premise: Zephyrine Okafor, a pest controller in the fading town of Hollowmere, is called to a farmhouse where something leaves human fingerprints on the ceilings. His documentation habit—photographs, measurements, careful notes—becomes a shield against a truth he cannot afford: the visitor is Wren, his childhood imaginary friend, unchanged after thirty years, and Wren has been keeping the town's founders' ritual alive by feeding it. When Zephyrine learns the harvest moon will complete what the founders abandoned, he must choose between exposing Hollowmere's founding crime or finishing the ritual himself, binding Wren and the town's dead into the soil forever. He finishes it, at the cost of being remembered by no one, surviving as the town's invisible keeper.
about_author: Noor Amberdale is the pen name of a former rural building inspector who spent a decade documenting structures no one wanted to enter. They write horror about people whose jobs require them to look closely at things that would rather not be seen.

chapters.title: Call Sheet
chapters.summary: Zephyrine Okafor takes a routine pest call at the Delacroix farmhouse on Hollowmere's edge, finding droppings that are too large and too deliberate. In the attic he photographs handprints pressed into the rafters—human-sized, five-fingered, warm to the touch. POV: Zephyrine. Emotional beat: professional calm stretched over a first hairline crack of dread.

chapters.title: Documentation Is a Kind of Prayer
chapters.summary: Back home, Zephyrine catalogs the evidence with obsessive care, revealing through flashbacks how note-taking steadied him after a childhood of being overlooked. His sister Adaeze warns him the Delacroix job smells like the old Hollowmere stories. POV: Zephyrine. Emotional beat: the comfort of ritual shadowed by the sense that recording something can also invite it.

chapters.title: The Porch
chapters.summary: Returning for a follow-up visit, Zephyrine finds a small figure waiting on the porch steps: Wren, his imaginary friend from age seven, unchanged, patient, and real. Wren speaks only in phrases Zephyrine once invented. POV: Zephyrine. Emotional beat: vertiginous joy curdling into terror—the past has been standing still, waiting.

chapters.title: What the Founders Buried
chapters.summary: In the county archive, Zephyrine discovers Hollowmere's founding families sealed an agreement in 1891—a covenant written in blood-ink, promising 'the harvest's tithe.' The last signature page is torn out. POV: Zephyrine, with archival documents interleaved. Emotional beat: scholarly curiosity giving way to complicity; his hometown was built on a debt.

chapters.title: Fingerprints
chapters.summary: The Delacroix family reports their daughter talking to someone named Wren. Zephyrine matches the child's drawings to his own childhood sketches, stroke for stroke. He realizes Wren attaches to isolated children—and always has. POV: alternating Zephyrine and young Maisie Delacroix. Emotional beat: protective urgency; history is repeating inside another family.

chapters.title: Adaeze's Warning
chapters.summary: Adaeze confronts Zephyrine with their grandmother's stories: the Okafor family came to Hollowmere as outsiders and were never fully counted among the founders—which may be why they survived. She begs him to leave before the harvest moon. POV: Adaeze. Emotional beat: love expressed as anger; belonging has always had a price tag.

chapters.title: Wren Explains Nothing
chapters.summary: Wren appears in Zephyrine's apartment, sitting exactly where he sat thirty years ago, and answers every question with riddles about 'keeping the count.' Zephyrine realizes Wren isn't haunting him—he's recruiting him. POV: Zephyrine. Emotional beat: the ache of reunion poisoned by manipulation; some friendships were never innocent.

chapters.title: The Tithe Ledger
chapters.summary: Following Wren's clues, Zephyrine finds a ledger hidden in the farmhouse well listing names across 130 years—one per harvest, each marked 'paid' or 'carried.' The carried names are children who grew up and left. The paid names stopped in 1994. POV: Zephyrine. Emotional beat: cold arithmetic of survival; the town has been buying time with its own.

chapters.title: Hollowmere Remembers
chapters.summary: Town elders, led by matriarch Odile Fontenot, quietly warn businesses to close early as the moon waxes. Zephyrine notices residents avoiding his eyes—they know what he's found. POV: rotating townsfolk vignettes. Emotional beat: communal guilt; everyone suspects, no one asks, and silence is the town's oldest tradition.

chapters.title: Maisie's Friend
chapters.summary: Maisie goes missing overnight and returns unharmed but speaking in Wren's borrowed phrases. Her parents, terrified, blame Zephyrine and bar him from the property. POV: Maisie. Emotional beat: innocence weaponized; the reader sees Wren through a child's adoring eyes and understands his power completely.

chapters.title: The Torn Page
chapters.summary: Odile Fontenot summons Zephyrine and produces the torn signature page, kept by her family for generations. The final signatory was an Okafor ancestor who refused to pay and cursed the covenant to hunger instead. POV: Odile. Emotional beat: reluctant alliance; two families' inherited sins finally face each other across a kitchen table.

chapters.title: Carried
chapters.summary: Zephyrine decodes the ledger: 'carried' children like himself weren't spared—they were deferred, marked as future payment. Wren has been his keeper and his collector all along. POV: Zephyrine. Emotional beat: betrayal at the deepest level; the friend who made lonely childhood bearable was a leash.

chapters.title: Ritual Fragments
chapters.summary: Piecing together the founders' rite from the ledger, the covenant, and Wren's riddles, Zephyrine learns the ritual must be finished at the standing stones beyond the farm—or the hunger will take the whole town when the moon rises. POV: Zephyrine. Emotional beat: grim clarity; there is no clean exit, only a choice of debts.

chapters.title: The Founders' Descendants
chapters.summary: Zephyrine gathers the five descendant families to finish what their ancestors started. Half refuse, insisting the covenant is superstition; one elder confesses her father fed the tithe a drifter in 1961. POV: ensemble scene anchored by Zephyrine. Emotional beat: justice outside the law—no court can try these crimes, so the living must answer for them.

chapters.title: First Frost
chapters.summary: Signs accelerate: livestock found arranged in circles, frost patterns spelling the ledger's names on windows, Wren visible now to everyone. The refusing families begin to disappear one by one. POV: Zephyrine and Adaeze. Emotional beat: panic under pressure; disbelief dies hard and fast.

chapters.title: What Wren Was Before
chapters.summary: At the stones, Zephyrine uncovers bones of the covenant's first victim—a founder's illegitimate child, erased from every record, whose loneliness became the thing called Wren. Wren was never imaginary; he was forgotten so thoroughly he became a hunger. POV: Zephyrine. Emotional beat: devastating empathy; the monster is what the town does to the unwanted.

chapters.title: The Offer
chapters.summary: On the eve of the harvest moon, Wren offers Zephyrine a bargain: walk away, be 'carried' again, live long and unseen, and let the town pay. Zephyrine, who has spent his life invisible, feels the offer's terrible sweetness. POV: Zephyrine. Emotional beat: temptation rendered honestly; survival has always been his native language.

chapters.title: Harvest Moon Rising
chapters.summary: The remaining descendants gather at the stones as the moon crests. The ritual requires a name freely given into the count. The town watches from the fields, unable to intervene, unwilling to look away. POV: Zephyrine. Emotional beat: ceremonial dread; the climax begins not with violence but with a question—who pays?

chapters.title: The Count
chapters.summary: Climax: Zephyrine gives his own name, seizing the ledger and rewriting the covenant—binding Wren, the founders' debt, and himself into the soil together. Wren, offered at last a witness rather than a meal, accepts. The hunger closes like a book. POV: Zephyrine. Emotional beat: sacrificial transcendence; justice achieved by stepping into the wound.

chapters.title: Unwritten
chapters.summary: Dawn. The town wakes with no memory of Zephyrine Okafor—his records blank, his photos empty, his name gone from every document except the buried ledger. Only Maisie, half-dreaming, draws a man with kind tired eyes and cannot say why she cries. POV: Maisie and Adaeze. Emotional beat: grief without an object; erasure as both punishment and mercy.

chapters.title: The Keeper
chapters.summary: A new pest controller arrives in Hollowmere years later, following rumors of a farmhouse that maintains itself. On the porch sits a small figure, waiting patiently, keeping the count—and somewhere beneath the stones, something documented everything, because documentation is a kind of prayer. POV: the newcomer, then Zephyrine's voice in the final pages. Emotional beat: cyclical unease laced with peace; the price was paid, and payment never truly ends.

chapters.title: Appendix: Field Notes
chapters.summary: Epistolary coda: recovered field notes in an unknown hand describe the Delacroix house, the porch, and a promise kept, dated across decades yet written in one lifetime's handwriting. The final entry reads simply: 'He stayed. That was the whole ritual.' POV: documentary fragments. Emotional beat: quiet devastation; the reader holds the only proof Zephyrine ever existed.
